dedupe_keys.name: a worldwide event based debris flow barrier dam dataset from 1800 to 2023

description: The Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment publishes a worldwide event database of debris-flow barrier dams formed between 1800 and 2023. The researchers assembled 555 documented events after reviewing 2,519 publications and media reports. Each entry can contain up to 38 attributes, including location, trigger, formation date, debris-flow velocity, dam dimensions, impounded-lake properties, longevity, failure mechanism and peak discharge. Zenodo lists an XLSX workbook under CC-BY-4.0 with open, free access. These are natural blockages produced by debris flows, not an inventory of engineered dams. Historical reporting, missing measurements and differences in reliability limit statistical interpretation. Infrastructure modellers could use the events to develop blockage or outburst-flood scenarios near roads, bridges, settlements and water infrastructure. The data complement engineered dam inventories by describing a different source of impoundment and downstream flood hazard. Any fitted relationship should account for event selection and attribute uncertainty instead of treating every historical value as a direct measurement.
